# Memory Hierarchy & Bandwidth: Cache, Arithmetic Intensity, Roofline Model ## First Principle: Bandwidth = Throughput **Bandwidth** is how much data can move per second. ``` Example: NVLink between two GPUs Bandwidth: 900 GB/s (gigabytes per second) What this means: In 1 second, 900 billion bytes can move In 1 millisecond, 900 million bytes (900 MB) In 1 microsecond, 900 KB ``` **Why does bandwidth matter?** If your algorithm moves lots of data, bandwidth is your bottleneck. ``` Example: Matrix transpose Read 1 billion floats (4 GB) Write 1 billion floats (4 GB) Total: 8 GB moved On NVLink (900 GB/s): 8 GB / 900 GB/s = 8.9 ms On PCIe (32 GB/s): 8 GB / 32 GB/s = 250 ms PCIe is 28x slower (same operation) ``` --- ## Arithmetic Intensity: FLOPs per Byte **Arithmetic intensity** measures how much computation happens per byte of data moved. ``` Arithmetic Intensity (AI) = FLOPs / Bytes Transferred Example 1: Simple add for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) c[i] = a[i] + b[i]; FLOPs: n (one add per iteration) Bytes: 3n floats (read a[i], read b[i], write c[i]) * 4 bytes = 12n bytes AI = n / 12n = 1/12 FLOP/byte Example 2: Matrix multiply C = A * B (512x512) FLOPs: 512 * 512 * 512 * 2 (MAC) = 256M FLOPs Bytes: 512*512 floats read from A + B + 512*512 written to C = 1.5M floats * 4 = 6M bytes AI = 256M / 6M = 42 FLOPs/byte (HIGH) Example 3: Stencil (image filter) for each pixel: output = sum of 9 neighbors (one 3x3 box) FLOPs: 9 adds per pixel Bytes: 9 reads (9 neighbors) * 4 bytes = 36 bytes AI = 9 / 36 = 0.25 FLOPs/byte (LOW) ``` --- ## The Roofline Model: Finding Your Bottleneck **Roofline model** shows whether your code is **compute-bound** or **memory-bound**. The idea: your throughput is limited by either: 1. **Peak compute** (GFLOPs/s), or 2. **Bandwidth** (GB/s) * arithmetic intensity ``` Throughput = min(Peak Compute, Bandwidth * Arithmetic Intensity) ``` **Visual:** ```mermaid graph LR A["Peak Compute
312 TFLOPS
H100 GPU"] B["Memory Bandwidth
2 TB/s
H100 GPU"] C["Arithmetic Intensity
FLOPs per Byte"] D["Achieved Throughput
min of compute/bandwidth"] A --> D B --> D C --> D style D fill:#fff9c4 ``` **Deriving the boundary:** ``` When is compute the bottleneck? Peak Compute = Bandwidth * AI 312 TFLOPS = 2 TB/s * AI 312 * 10^12 FLOPS/s = 2 * 10^12 bytes/s * AI AI = 312 / 2 = 156 FLOPS/byte When AI > 156: compute is the bottleneck (you can't feed the GPU fast enough) When AI < 156: memory is the bottleneck (you're waiting for data) ``` **The roofline diagram:** ``` Throughput (FLOPS) | 312T |────────── COMPUTE BOUND (peak compute) |╱ |╱ Memory-bound region (slope = bandwidth) |╱ 0+────────────────── Arithmetic Intensity (FLOPS/byte) 0 156 ``` **Concrete examples:** ``` Example 1: Simple add (AI = 1/12) ├─ Peak compute: 312 TFLOPS ├─ Bandwidth * AI: 2 TB/s * (1/12) FLOPS/byte = 166 GFLOPS └─ Achieved throughput: min(312T, 166G) = 166G (MEMORY-BOUND) Example 2: Matrix multiply (AI = 42) ├─ Peak compute: 312 TFLOPS ├─ Bandwidth * AI: 2 TB/s * 42 FLOPS/byte = 84 TFLOPS └─ Achieved throughput: min(312T, 84T) = 84T (MEMORY-BOUND, but better) Example 3: Small matrix multiply (fits in shared memory, AI = 200) ├─ Peak compute: 312 TFLOPS ├─ Bandwidth * AI: 2 TB/s * 200 FLOPS/byte = 400 TFLOPS └─ Achieved throughput: min(312T, 400T) = 312T (COMPUTE-BOUND, full GPU) ``` --- ## Real Example: Attention Kernel (KV-Cache) **Problem:** Computing attention for vLLM inference. ``` Input: Q (query): 1 token (128 dimensions) * 2 bytes = 256 bytes K (key): 4K context (128 dims) * 2 bytes = 1 MB V (value): 4K context (128 dims) * 2 bytes = 1 MB Computation: scores = Q @ K^T → 1 x 4K matmul attn_weights = softmax(scores) → 4K values output = attn_weights @ V → 4K x 128 matmul FLOPs: Q @ K^T: 1 * 4K * 128 * 2 = 1M FLOPs softmax: 4K * 10 ops = 40K FLOPs attn @ V: 4K * 128 * 2 = 1M FLOPs Total: ~2M FLOPs Data movement: Read Q: 256 bytes Read K: 1 MB Read V: 1 MB Write output: 128 * 2 = 256 bytes Total: 2M bytes Arithmetic Intensity: AI = 2M FLOPs / 2M bytes = 1 FLOP/byte Analysis: Bandwidth * AI: 2 TB/s * 1 = 2 TFLOPS (MEMORY-BOUND) Peak compute: 312 TFLOPS Bottleneck: MEMORY (K and V fetches dominate) Solution: Reduce data movement by caching K and V in shared memory Or: use KV-cache quantization (4x less memory) ``` --- ## Why Decode is Slow (vLLM Example) ``` Prefill (processing prompt): Q: 4K tokens, K: 4K tokens, V: 4K tokens Matrix size: 4K x 4K attention AI = 8 FLOPs/byte (compute-bound) GPU utilization: 100% Time: 100ms Decode (generating next token): Q: 1 token, K: 4K tokens, V: 4K tokens Matrix size: 1 x 4K attention AI = 1 FLOP/byte (memory-bound) GPU utilization: 10% Time: 10ms per token Insight: Decode reads 4K context but only computes 1 token. Most of the GPU sits idle waiting for memory. This is why batching helps: batch 32 tokens, 32x more compute on same memory. ``` --- ## Bandwidth Hierarchy (Different Levels) ```mermaid graph TD A["GPU Registers

Minimize global memory accesses (most common bottleneck) 2. Maximize shared memory reuse 3. Avoid PCIe/network transfers if possible --- ## Strategy: Roofline-Driven Optimization Given a kernel that's memory-bound: **Option 1: Increase arithmetic intensity** ``` Original: AI = 1 FLOP/byte (memory-bound) Goal: AI > 156 (to become compute-bound) Strategy: Reduce memory transfers Use shared memory to cache data (reuse) Fuse operations (combine multiple kernels) Example: fuse attention + linear projection Before: attention reads V (1M), writes (256), linear reads output (256), writes (256) After: attention computes, passes directly to linear (avoids 256 byte write/read) Memory saved: 256 bytes per token ``` **Option 2: Reduce data movement** ``` Example: KV-cache quantization Before: 4K context * 128 dims * 2 bytes = 1 MB per request After: 4K context * 128 dims * 0.5 bytes (INT8) = 0.25 MB Bandwidth savings: 4x New AI: 1 FLOP/byte * 4 = 4 FLOPs/byte (still memory-bound, but better) ``` **Option 3: Batch to hide latency** ``` Single token: 1 token, AI = 1, throughput = 2 GFLOPS (10% GPU) Batch 32: 32 tokens, AI = 32, throughput = 64 GFLOPS (100% GPU) Same memory bandwidth, but amortized across more compute ``` --- ## Story Card: vLLM Continuous Batching **Setup:** vLLM serves Llama-70B. Decode is memory-bound (10% GPU utilization). **Problem:** 1 token at a time → 10% utilization → can serve ~10 requests/sec at $100/hr. **Solution:** Continuous batching ``` Old: Process 1 token per batch Memory: 1 token, K 4K (1 MB), V 4K (1 MB) → AI = 1 Throughput: 2 GFLOPS Time: 5 ms per batch New: Process 32 tokens per batch Memory: 32 tokens, K 4K (1 MB), V 4K (1 MB) → AI = 32 Throughput: 64 GFLOPS (same memory bandwidth, 32x more FLOPS) Time: 5 ms per batch (still limited by K/V fetch) But now process 32 tokens in 5 ms = 6.4 tokens/ms = 32 requests/sec Improvement: 3.2x more throughput, 100% GPU utilization ``` **Key insight:** Roofline told us the bottleneck. Continuous batching increases AI, saturating the GPU. --- ## Q&A (Built on Fundamentals) **Recall 1:** What is arithmetic intensity? Give an example where it's high (> 10) and low (< 1). *Must-say:* - Arithmetic intensity = FLOPs / bytes moved - High: matrix multiply (many FLOPs per byte) - Low: memory copy (1 FLOP per byte... actually 0, just copying) **Probe 1:** A kernel has AI = 0.5 FLOPS/byte. GPU bandwidth is 2 TB/s. Peak compute is 312 TFLOPS. What's your bottleneck? *Expected:* - Bandwidth * AI = 2 TB/s * 0.5 = 1 TFLOPS - Peak compute: 312 TFLOPS - min(1T, 312T) = 1T → MEMORY-BOUND - Optimization: reduce memory transfers (quantization, caching) **Probe 2:** You're implementing an attention kernel. Prefill is compute-bound (100% GPU). Decode is memory-bound (10% GPU). Why? How do you fix it? *Expected:* - Prefill: batched matmul (many tokens * many tokens = high AI) - Decode: 1 token * many tokens = low AI (memory-bound) - Fix: batch decode (continuous batching, multiple requests) **Numeric 1:** Matrix multiply: A is 512x512, B is 512x512, C = A*B. How many FLOPs? How many bytes moved? *Working:* - FLOPs: 512 * 512 * 512 * 2 = 268M FLOPs - Bytes: 512*512 floats from A (1M) + 512*512 from B (1M) + output (1M) = 3M floats * 4 = 12M bytes - AI = 268M / 12M = 22 FLOPs/byte - Bandwidth * AI = 2 TB/s * 22 = 44 TFLOPS (memory-bound) **Numeric 2:** Decode: 1 query token, 4K context. Attention is 1x4K matmul. FLOPs? *Working:* - FLOPs: 1 * 4K * 128 * 2 = 1M FLOPs - Bytes: 1 query (256B) + 4K context K (1M) + 4K context V (1M) = 2M bytes - AI = 1M / 2M = 0.5 FLOPs/byte (very memory-bound) --- ## Questions for the Interviewer - How do you measure roofline for your kernels? (NVIDIA Nsight, custom profiling?) - Have you optimized a memory-bound kernel by increasing arithmetic intensity? - In your system, what's the AI of the critical path? (compute vs memory bound?) - How do you handle kernels that are memory-bound but can't be batched further?
